intro: Excavator operators control heavy machines precisely and watch conditions closely, skills used across construction, mining and rail. The closest of the 25 careers below is construction equipment operation, with a 93% match, while Pile Driver Operators are 90% matched and earn a BLS May 2025 median of $73,300, or 28% more.
why_it_works: Digging and loading at a mine or quarry means reading the ground, moving huge loads safely and keeping equipment in working order. O*NET rates operation and control at 4.12 out of 5 for this job, and operations monitoring at 3.62. Pile driving, hoisting and paving use the same control skills. Almost every match needs no extra schooling. The gaps are maintenance and installation.
tips: Power-line work pays the most here: installers earn $95,320, which is 66% more.
Locomotive Engineers earn $81,410, or 42% more, and railroads train new hires.
Learn basic equipment maintenance; operators who can fix their machines are in demand.

faq.q: What jobs can former excavator operators do?
faq.a: The closest matches are construction equipment operators (93%), Pile Driver Operators (90%) and Hoist and Winch Operators (89%), based on O*NET 31.0. Construction equipment operators earn $59,850, which is 4% more than the $57,430 median for excavating and dragline operators.

faq.q: Which careers for excavator operators pay more?
faq.a: 14 of the 25 matches pay more. Power-line installers earn $95,320 (66% more), Locomotive Engineers $81,410 (42% more) and Terrazzo Workers and Finishers $76,170 (33% more), according to BLS May 2025 data. Line and rail jobs train through paid programs.

faq.q: Do excavator operators need more education to switch?
faq.a: Rarely. 23 of the 25 matches need no more education than excavating machine operators already have, including 9 of the top 10. In the closest match, 82% of workers have a high school diploma or the equivalent, and most training happens on the job.

faq.q: What skills should excavator operators learn?
faq.a: The skills that most often need work are equipment maintenance, installation, complex problem solving and instructing. Coordination already rates 3 out of 5 for this job in O*NET, so maintaining machines and training new operators are the main steps up.
